heroHeadline: Ukraine Fortifies Chernobyl Zone Against Belarus Invasion Threat as Rada Weighs $1.1B Decommissioning Extension
heroSubtitle: A Der Spiegel investigation reported August 10 that Ukrainian forces have dug trenches, built defensive tunnels, and strung anti-drone nets across the exclusion zone's northern reaches near the Belarusian border, guarding against a possible renewed Russian advance. Separately, Ukraine's Cabinet submitted a bill to the Verkhovna Rada on August 9 extending the Chornobyl decommissioning and Shelter transformation programme through 2036, with UAH 50.8B (~$1.1B) in funding including repairs for New Safe Confinement damage from the February 2025 drone strike.
footerNote: Data sourced from IAEA, UNSCEAR, WHO, Ukrainian government archives, Soviet/Russian state archives, Chernobyl Forum (2005), TORCH Report (2006), and peer-reviewed research.
